newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Centam to ask U.S. not to raise Mexico sugar quota.
newsitem.headline: Centam to ask U.S. not to raise Mexico sugar quota.

text.p: Central American sugar producers plan to ask the United States not to raise Mexico's export quotas, saying greater trade with Mexico will hurt their sugar exports.
The request will be prepared by Central American ambassadors in Washington on the behalf of regional sugar producers, Honduras Industry, Trade and Tourism Minister Fernando Garcia said Monday.

Central American sugar producers have expressed their concern that higher Mexican sugar quotas, outlined in North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA), will reduce demand for their sugar, a key crop for the region.

"If Mexico succeeds in this manuever and it removes part of the Central American quota, we will lose sales to the United States of 30,000 tonnes," executive director of the Central American Sugar Agriculture Industry Jose Orive told Reuters.
Mexico is limited to 25,000 tonnes of exports to the United States until the year 2001, when the quota will be lifted to 100,000 tonnes. In 2010, the quota is scheduled to be removed.
Mexico and the United States are discussing possible adjustment of the quotas, a Mexico's Sugar Industry Chamber spokesman said in Mexico City.
He said the chamber wants to raise Mexican sugar cane exports from a limit of 25,000 tonnes per year to counter imports into Mexico of U.S. high fructose corn syrup, of about 300,000 tonnes.
